cards.text: Pull up a stool, friend, because we're hitting the road with Jesus and His disciples. The day of His ascension is getting close, and Jesus resolutely sets out for Jerusalem.

Jesus sends messengers on ahead into a village of the Samaritans to make arrangements for Him. That's an advance team, friend, while the rest of us just pull into the driveway and text "outside" like that's a whole PLAN.

cards.question: The people in the Samaritan village refuse to welcome Jesus because He is heading for ___.

cards.text: James and John, two of Jesus' disciples, see all this. And they ask Jesus a question that is, uh… a LOT.

cards.question: James and John ask Jesus if He wants them to call down ___ from heaven to consume the people of that Samaritan village.
True or false: When James and John ask about calling down fire on the Samaritan village, Jesus turns and rebukes them.
True or false: After Jesus rebukes James and John, He and His disciples stay in the Samaritan village.

cards.text: So they go on to another village, and as they're walking along the road, someone says to Jesus, “I will follow You wherever You go.” WHEREVER is a big word, friend.

cards.question: Jesus tells the man who will follow Him wherever that foxes have dens and birds of the air have nests. What does He say about the Son of Man, His name for Himself (Mark 2:10)?

answers.text: He has no place to lay His head
He has a home waiting in Jerusalem
He has a house in every town

cards.text: Then Jesus says to another man, “Follow Me.” The man replies, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.”

cards.question: Jesus answers the man who wants to bury his father first, “Let the dead bury their own dead.” Then what does Jesus tell this man to go and do?

cards.text: Then still another man speaks up: “I will follow You, Lord; but first…” There's that word AGAIN.

cards.question: True or false: Still another man says he'll follow Jesus, but first he asks to say farewell to his family.

cards.text: Jesus answers him with a picture from the field: a man who puts his hand to the plow. Friend, the only thing I've ever pushed is dough, and even THAT gets away from me.

cards.question: In Jesus' picture, what does the man at the plow do that makes him not fit for the kingdom of God?
